paragraphs: Brass became the material of precision mechanisms because it machines cleanly, does not rust and wears against steel without seizing. Every clock, instrument and early calculating machine used it, which is why the colour now reads as engineering rather than as decoration.
The model holds 75,976 polygons and 74,245 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $69 it suits technology and engineering illustration, museum and exhibition work, steampunk and period scenes, advertising, film props, game environments and editorial work. On sale since 2021.

A glass facade is a decision about privacy before it is a decision about light. The whole architectural argument of the contemporary house is that the boundary between inside and garden should be as thin as structure allows, and everything else in the design follows from defending that.
The model is light at 34,417 polygons and 39,568 vertices, built in quads only with overlapping UVs, so it drops easily into wide scenes. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $69 it suits architectural and residential visualisation, property marketing, landscape scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Packing machines are judged on how gently they handle things at speed. The mechanism has to place a cover, seat it and move on several times a minute without marking the product, which is a far harder specification than simply doing it quickly.
The model holds 131,950 polygons and 138,727 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $69 it suits manufacturing and packaging visualisation, equipment marketing, production line scenes, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2024.

A curve is the hard part of any conveyor. The outer edge has to travel further than the inner one, so the rollers are tapered or driven at different rates, and a package that arrives square has to leave square or the whole line downstream jams.
The model holds 96,360 polygons and 105,439 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $69 it suits warehouse and logistics visualisation, materials handling marketing, factory and distribution scenes, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2021.

The abra is the cheapest way to cross Dubai Creek and has been for a century. A wooden hull, a bench down each side, a diesel engine at the back and a fare so small that the boats still run continuously while everything around them was rebuilt.

The model holds 149,838 polygons and 81,332 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in aged condition. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a newer build is offered separately.
At $69 it suits cultural and tourism visualisation, urban waterfront scenes, documentary and education work, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

A domestic embroidery machine is a small industrial robot that happens to sit on a table. The hoop moves in two axes under a needle that stays put, which is the same principle as a plotter, and the screen on the front is where the design is actually chosen.

The model is light at 40,108 polygons and 21,076 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the screen on, and comes rigged so the hoop and arm can be posed or animated. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and native rigged builds for Maya and Cinema 4D are offered separately.
At $69 it suits product and craft equipment visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, workshop and interior scenes, and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The block is the one part of an engine that everything else bolts to, and the piston is the part that does the work. A collection separating them is how the four stroke cycle gets explained, because the motion only makes sense once you can see the bore it happens in.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the parts as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $69 the set suits automotive engineering visualisation, technical and training material, parts catalogues, education, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

The hood was never for the executioner's shame, whatever the films suggest. It was for his safety: in a small town the man who did the job had to go home afterwards, and anonymity was the only thing that made that possible.
The model is supplied as the mask on a head, in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification.
At $69 it suits historical and film costume work, horror and thriller production, game characters, concept art, museum material and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The wrist mounted computer is retro futurism at its most literal: a machine imagined by a past that expected the future to be built from vacuum tubes and toggle switches. Strapped to a forearm, it reads instantly as survival equipment rather than as a gadget.
The model holds 51,948 polygons and 52,893 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied fitted to the arm, and carries StemCell certification.
At $69 it suits game characters and props, science fiction film and animation, concept art, fan illustration, cosplay reference and editorial work. On sale since 2024.

The bearded sage is one of the oldest character shorthands there is. Length signals time, and time signals knowledge, which is why the wizard, the prophet and the master craftsman all ended up looking the same in every tradition that has one.
The model holds 32,370 polygons and 54,517 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, supplied as a head. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $69 it suits character development and sculpting reference, game and film assets, fantasy illustration, concept art and editorial work. On sale since 2026.

A curtain sider is the compromise between a box and a flatbed. The sides roll back so a forklift can load from either edge, and the roof still keeps the weather off, which is why so much palletised freight travels this way rather than through a rear door.
The model holds 237,502 polygons and 240,926 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in white. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $69 it suits logistics and haulage visualisation, fleet and livery mockups, industrial and street scenes, advertising, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

Desert art is built to be seen after dark. There is nothing else out there to light it, so the sculpture has to carry its own glow, and the work is designed around how it reads at night rather than how it looks at noon.
The model holds 77,058 polygons and 78,450 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $69 it suits festival and event visualisation, art and installation presentation, night scenes, advertising, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A multiday pack is a suspension system with a bag attached. The frame, the hip belt and the harness carry the weight onto the pelvis, and the fabric part is almost incidental, which is why fitting one properly matters more than what it is made of.
The model holds 37,265 polygons and 37,713 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in blue. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $69 it suits outdoor and retail visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, advertising, character accessories, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A desk model on a stand is a different object from the aircraft it depicts. It exists to sit in an office, and the proportions are usually flattered slightly, because a scale model that is strictly accurate rarely looks as good as one that is not.
The model is very light at 9,502 polygons and 9,524 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied with its stand. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.

At $69 it suits interior and office visualisation, product and collectible imagery, aviation and defence presentation, film set dressing, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.
